text: Which projects use the wave-like motion of atoms as the measuring element in high-precision sensors of gravity and acceleration?
reference_answer: Six projects use atom (matter-wave) interferometry as the measuring element for precision gravity and acceleration measurement, spanning instrument building, sensitivity theory and commercial translation. MWGRAV pursued matter-wave gravitation sensors at SYRTE, noting that atom interferometers already compete with or beat inertial sensors built on other technologies, and targeting gravimetry, gradiometry, metrology and gravitational-wave detection. Dommigs designed a monolithic reflective interferometer with diffraction slabs cut into a silicon monolith, evaluated for prospecting gravimetry and for accelerometers for long-distance under-water navigation. TICTOCGRAV combined ultracold Cadmium and Strontium optical clocks with Bragg interferometers, aiming at tests of the weak equivalence principle below 10^-13, while MEGANTE probed the gravitational field with cold atoms in free fall to redetermine the gravitational constant G beyond torsion-balance and pendulum accuracy. On the enhancement and translation side, QBAS investigated theoretically how entanglement between atoms and photons could raise atom-interferometer sensitivity, pointing at gravity gradiometers for detecting mineral reserves, and SEQ funded an engineer at M Squared Lasers to develop a first-iteration magneto-optical trap into a stable atom interferometer and commercialise a gravimeter.
notes: SEEDS: candidate cp6 vector-55 (atom/matter-wave interferometry as inertial and gravity sensor). Drift check re-ran the candidate SQL (objective/title ILIKE '%atom interferomet%') -> same 6 ids (660081 MWGRAV, 691156 Q-Sense, 704672 QBAS, 739651 SEQ, 804815 MEGANTE, 101031712 Dommigs). TWO SEPARATE UNIVERSES, DO NOT CONFLATE: (a) the POOLED UNION recorded in pooling_evidence - one k=20 run of all four conditions, 32 distinct projects; (b) the REGEX COMPLETENESS SWEEP below - a non-embedding SQL universe of 28 projects that exists to prove no satisfying project went unadjudicated. They overlap in 13 projects; the adjudicated union across both is 47 projects, of which 6 are gold. COMPLETENESS SWEEP (regexp_matches, case-folded, over project.title + project.objective + report_text.teaser/summary/workPerformed/finalResults concatenated per project): patterns 'atom[ -]?interferomet' (8 projects), 'matter[ -]?wave interferomet|matterwave interferomet' (5), 'matter[ -]?wave|matterwave' (25), 'cold[ -]?atom' (156), '(atomic|atom|quantum|cold[ -]?atom)[ -]?(gravimet|gradiomet)' (6), 'gravimet|gradiomet' (92), 'inertial sensor|inertial navigation|accelerometer|gyroscope' (178), 'atom[ -]?chip|bose[ -]?einstein condensate|ultra[ -]?cold atom' (120). Swept universe = union of the targeted patterns plus (cold-atom/BEC family AND gravimet/gradiomet/inertial/interferomet family) = 28 projects; sweeping report_text added 772126 TICTOCGRAV and 894590 QSPACE, which the candidate's objective-only probe could not see. POOLING ARITHMETIC: pooled_candidate_count 32 = distinct projects in the k=20 pooled union; rejected_count 26 = union minus accepted, per the batch convention. Note for the re-deriver: 739651 SEQ is gold but appears in NO condition's top-20, so the pooled union itself contains 5 gold projects and 27 rejected ones; the 6th gold comes from the sweep. IN (6): 660081 MWGRAV - atom interferometers as inertial sensors for gravimetry, gradiometry, gravitational-wave detection; 704672 QBAS - entanglement to raise atom-interferometer sensitivity for accelerations and gravity gradiometry; 739651 SEQ - magneto-optical trap developed into a stable atom interferometer to conduct gravity measurements and commercialise a gravimeter; 772126 TICTOCGRAV - atomic gravimeters and Bragg interferometers, finalResults calls them measurements of gravity, gravity gradients and inertial sensing; 804815 MEGANTE - cold atoms in free fall probing the gravitational field to measure G, finalResults calls matter-wave atom interferometers established devices for measuring gravity and gravity gradients; 101031712 Dommigs - monolithic matter-wave interferometer for gravity sensing and navigation. DELIBERATE NEAR-MISSES (OUT, with reason, 10): 691156 Q-Sense - a promotion and translation action whose deliverables are satellite-mission plans, an open-source simulation toolbox and outreach to over 70 companies; its own executed measurement is the SOC2 strontium optical clock at 3 parts in 10^18, so its measuring instrument is a clock and atom interferometry appears as mission planning and tooling rather than an operated sensing element - excluded under the same bar as QUESCA and QSPACE; 894590 QSPACE - atom-interferometry technique appears only inside a microgravity quantum-memory protocol, the project builds quantum memories for satellite communication; 750017 QUESCA - cold-atom sensor squeezing via cavity-aided Faraday rotation, inertial sensing and gravimetry named only as downstream applications, no atomic interference as the measuring element; 832250 PhoQuS-G - senses gravitational fields with phonons in a BEC, not with the wave-like motion of the atoms; 801221 NEWTON-g - develops a MEMS gravimeter array alongside a quantum absolute gravimeter, the atom-based instrument is a reference anchor not the project's own sensing work; 658253 QuantuM-nano - hybrid gyroscope where the optical Sagnac effect is enhanced by slow light in a BEC, sensing element is the photonic circuit and the quantity is rotation; 654532 NANO-Q - matter-wave interferometry with nanoparticles to test macroscopicity, not atoms and not gravity sensing; 748826 ANGRAM - antihydrogen free-fall measured with a three-grating moire deflectometer, explicitly needing neither position resolution nor time-of-flight, a fundamental-physics test rather than an atomic-wave sensor; 766900 TEQ - explicitly aims to surpass matter-wave interferometry using a trapped nanocrystal; 701264 InertialSensors - interferometric inertial sensors for gravitational-wave detectors built from laser interferometry, light not atoms. OTHER REJECTS (OUT, off-topic on their own text, 31): 647434 DOQS, 657439 TOP-DOL, 683341 CAtMolChip, 704832 TwUnaGas, 705269 SCOUTFermi2D, 757386 quMercury, 765075 LIMQUET, 820419 Qombs, 884900 QPAP, 964531 CRYST^3, 101023088 LASERLOOP, 101032523 QuProbe, 670168 NEWPHYS-MOLECULES (ultracold-gas many-body, quantum-optics, precision-spectroscopy, EDM or training projects with no gravity/acceleration sensing); 677548 MODULAR, 638765 Q-CEOM, 863132 IQLev, 101030987 LOREN, 101019712 GUANTUM, 101027183 NOVUS, 787520 QUANTUM-N (mechanical, optomechanical or levitated oscillators as the sensing element, not atoms); 866259 SILENT, 865816 OmniSens, 955515 SPIN, 802279 In Motion (optical, seismic or radar instrumentation); 633818 dasQ (ultrafast electron microscopy); 654339 QUTEMAG (optical magnetometers, magnetic fields not gravity); 716651 NEDM (neutron EDM with mercury magnetometry); 659301 SOUNDCONE (photon fluids); 801781 ModGravTrial, 646702 CosTesGrav, 639729 preQFT (theory and cosmology). TERM_STYLE: paraphrase - the question avoids every distinctive gold term ('atom interferometer', 'matter-wave', 'gravimeter', 'gradiometer', 'inertial sensor', 'cold atoms') and describes the mechanism as 'the wave-like motion of atoms' acting as a 'measuring element'. The rank matrix is mixed and is recorded as such: MWGRAV is dense-only (lexical null) and SEQ is found by nothing, but Dommigs (lexical 1), TICTOCGRAV (2), MEGANTE (6) and QBAS (8) do carry lexical ranks, driven by the generic shared words gravity/atoms/sensors/precision rather than by the avoided terms. SEED-RETRIEVED: 739651 SEQ appears in no condition's top-20; its text is dominated by MSCA recruitment language, and it is kept in gold because its objective states the atom-interferometer-for-gravity work verbatim (retrieval never decides truth).

text: Which projects are aimed specifically at preventing, or detecting at an early stage, the skin and tissue damage that long periods of unrelieved pressure inflict on bedridden or wheelchair-bound patients?
reference_answer: Six H2020 grants in this corpus are aimed at this problem, and most are sensing-plus-prevention systems rather than treatments. i-LiveRest (696939) and its successor grant LiveRest (830134) put impedance, pressure, temperature and humidity textile sensors on a wheelchair or mattress to score Tissue Viability in real time and then trigger the prevention strategy that suits the user and context; their target group is Spinal Cord Injury patients, 85% of whom develop such an injury. Qone (735302) does the equivalent for bedridden patients with a pressure-relieving mattress carrying temperature and pressure mapping sensors feeding a personalised risk-score algorithm, claiming roughly a 75% reduction in new cases. The two JUMPAIR grants (709595, 783594) build a smart anti-decubitus mattress system that remotely tracks known ulcer-activity biomarkers to raise early alerts to the hospital. STINTS (811965) is the research and training strand: it studies the biomechanical and biochemical pathways by which prolonged pressure and shear destroy skin integrity, in order to improve preventative aids such as mattresses and insoles, early-stage diagnosis through non-invasive biomarkers and sensors, and ultrasound therapy.
notes:
SEEDS: cp6 candidate vector-68 (pressure injury / bedsores). Candidate evidence SQL re-executed this pass: the five-synonym ILIKE probe over project.title/objective still returns 11, no drift. Seed ids read in full: 696939, 709595, 735302, 783594, 811965, 815769, 830134, 834049, 845756, 868392, 869943.

BOUNDARY, ON THE FACE OF THE QUESTION: the question asks for projects 'aimed specifically at' preventing or early-detecting this damage. That wording, not the notes, decides the two boundaries where a survey gold set leaks. (a) Projects that heal an existing chronic wound are out, because healing is neither prevention nor early detection: 815769 LYSADERM (platelet-lysate cream for skin ulcers, pressure ulcers one of three indications), 869943 DERMAREP (eggshell-membrane dressing for pressure, leg and diabetic foot ulcers). (b) Projects whose own aim is something else, and for which this damage is a downstream application, are out: 845756 BIOCONTACT states 'the main objective of BIOCONTACT was to develop an advanced contact mechanics model able to accurately describe the contact behavior of elastic/viscoelastic thin layers', and reaches bedsores only as one benefit among contact lenses and prosthetic bones ('the accurate prediction of the contacting normal and tangential stresses acting on the soft biological tissues provides an efficient tool to reduce bedsores in long-term bedridden patients'). Every gold member's own stated aim IS this damage: prevention systems (696939, 830134, 735302, 709595, 783594) or the study of how prolonged pressure and shear destroy skin integrity in order to improve prevention and early diagnosis (811965).

JUMPAIR: 709595 (SME Phase 1, 2016) and 783594 (SME Phase 2, 2018) are two separate grants with the same acronym and distinct objectives; both are separately funded projects whose text satisfies the question, so both are gold. Same treatment for the i-LiveRest (696939) / LiveRest (830134) pair.

POOLED ADJUDICATION (final question string, k=20, all four conditions, 38 distinct projects). IN (6): 696939 i-LiveRest (real-time Tissue Viability sensing to prevent PU in wheelchair users); 830134 LiveRest (same system, written throughout as Pressure Injury, never pressure ulcer); 735302 Qone (sensing mattress predicting and preventing PU in bedridden patients); 783594 JUMPAIR (smart anti-decubitus system, biomarker monitoring for early diagnosis and prevention); 709595 JUMPAIR (Phase 1 of the same anti-decubitus system); 811965 STINTS (skin tissue integrity under prolonged pressure and shear; objectives are preventative aids, early-stage diagnosis, therapy). OUT (32): 845756 BIOCONTACT, 815769 LYSADERM and 869943 DERMAREP per the boundary above (LYSADERM did not surface in this run's pool but is adjudicated in the sweep list); 868392 Dignum (toilet assistive device, pressure ulcers only an inspection feature); 101003407 ELECTROSKIN, 873123 SWORD, 885973 StrataGRT, 833594 PHAS, 955722 SkinTERM, 892407 SKIN-REGEN-MECH, 877901 Bio2Skin - wound-healing, skin-graft, bandage or skin-adhesive work with pressure ulcers at most named in a chronic-wound list; 849047 and 826930 AGLYC (cardiac ischemia), 801126 EDIT (bladder cancer), 836268 DermoSafe 2.0 (skin cancer), 839888 MultiBioScan (tissue glycation imaging), 840786 BrainWatch (intracranial pressure implants), 101031327 WEARSENSNANO (hypothermia monitoring), 101038096 NeuroVascularHealth, 812772 Phys2BioMed, 885435 MAIT, 853508 BARRIER BREAK, 848158 EarlyCause, 101029808 EarlyCare, 101017385 WARIFA, 645759 WASTCArD - other conditions, matched on 'early detection' or 'tissue'; 643853 SC0806, 956003 REPAIRS, 745431 MyTherapyTools, 872082 ImpHandRehab, 855081 ABLE, 689476 RELIEF - rehabilitation/paralysis projects that name such damage at most as a complication they do not work on; 867161 ROCS (ore composition monitoring) - off-domain lexical match. Total: 6 + 32 = 38.

COMPLETENESS SWEEP (regexp_matches, case-folded, over project.title+objective AND report_text teaser+summary+workPerformed+finalResults+title; unchanged by the rewording, since it sweeps the topic's vocabulary and not the question string). Pattern 1: 'pressure[ -]?(ulcer|injur|sore)|bed[ -]?sore|decubitus' -> 23 projects: the 11 that match in the project fields (the candidate's 11) plus 12 that match only in report text, adjudicated from their matched context - 653019 CEREBSENSING (robot lifting of bed-confined elderly as an example application), 665055 NETEEG (pressure injuries caused by long-worn dry EEG electrodes - device-borne, not immobility), 753633 ELECTRO-HEAL, 827096 SkinKer, 828092 BC SKIN, 873123 SWORD, 896904 Dual-NanoMAE, 101003407 ELECTROSKIN (chronic-wound healing materials listing pressure ulcers among indications), 828169 HeartWatch (bedsore prevention named as a future upgrade), 855081 ABLE, 899040 Neuroprosthesis-UI (pressure sores listed as a complication of paralysis), 959492 Klikkit (carer reminder platform) - all OUT. Pattern 2 (neighbouring vocabulary): 'tissue viability|bedridden|bed-ridden|bed bound|bedbound|prolonged (sitting|lying|immobil|bed)|repositioning|offload' AND 'skin|wound|ulcer|tissue|sore', excluding pattern-1 hits -> 13 projects: 637908 STIGMATICS, 737043 TISuMR, 752489 SODIUMMRI-4-EU, 759731 RECEIVE, 770889 ULTRA, 771883 XHaLe, 777072 INSIST, 822455 GENBIO, 871312 HandheldOCT, 875328 ChronicPain, 954353 Signia, 963865 MELASTOP, 101024448 STASIS - all OUT, none concerns pressure-induced tissue damage.

DELIBERATE NEAR-MISSES (sweep hits judged out, each decidable from the question's 'aimed specifically at' wording): 845756 BIOCONTACT, 815769 LYSADERM, 869943 DERMAREP, 834049 PODIUM (diabetic foot ulcer thermography; pressure ulcers only in a market-size sentence), 868392 Dignum, 665055 NETEEG, 828169 HeartWatch, 653019 CEREBSENSING, 855081 ABLE, 899040 Neuroprosthesis-UI.

TERM_STYLE: paraphrase. The question uses none of the vocabulary the gold texts use for the condition itself (pressure ulcer, PU, pressure injury, PI, decubitus ulcer, DeU, bedsore, pressure sore, tissue viability); it says 'the skin and tissue damage that long periods of unrelieved pressure inflict'. Rank matrix on the final string (lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank): 696939 = 1/1/1/2; 811965 = 2/2/2/1; 735302 = 3/3/3/4; 830134 = 19/6/4/3; 783594 = null/9/20/null; 709595 = null/11/null/null. The two decubitus-worded JUMPAIR grants are reachable only by dense/hybrid, the paraphrase signature; the three that lexical ranks high share only generic words (pressure, skin, tissue, bedridden, prevent, early), never the condition's name.

text: Which projects are developing chips or other dedicated hardware in which artificial neurons compute by firing brief pulses at each other, the way nerve cells do?
reference_answer: A cluster of H2020 projects builds computing hardware in which the signals are neuron-like pulses rather than clocked digital arithmetic. NeuRAM3 proposed to fabricate a chip implementing a neuromorphic architecture supporting spike-based learning, in FDSOI at 28nm design rules with RRAM synapses; MeM-Scales works on analog spiking microprocessors whose memory devices cover timescales spanning up to 9 orders of magnitude; SYNCH couples the brain of a living animal to a silicon neural network of spiking neurons on a chip through neuromorphic synapses; ULPEC connects a neuromorphic event-based camera to a Spiking Neural Network with memristive synapses; ChipAI builds resonant-tunnelling nanophotonic sources and detectors that fire and detect neuron-like light-spiking signals at >10 GHz per spike rates; NEPSpiNN puts event-based spiking processing of surface EMG into a compact ultra-low power neuromorphic chip; BeFerroSynaptic packaged TEXEL, a 9mm x 9mm neuromorphic chip carrying 180 adaptive-exponential integrate and fire (AdExp-I&F) neurons fed by ferroelectric synaptic devices; and TEMPO and ANDANTE develop the underlying technology and hardware platforms (integrate-and-fire engines, emerging memories, 3D integration, edge SNN chips). The same set also includes NANOINFER, whose intelligent memory chips combine digital CMOS logic with spiking neurons circuits, Fun-COMP, whose nanoelectronic and nanophotonic building blocks implement spiking neural networks in hardware, NeuroAgents, which fabricated the DYNAP-SE2 mixed-signal Spiking Neuronal Network processor for neuromorphic robotic agents, and SOFT, which designed, fabricated and tested a magnetic domain-wall spiking neuron and used a magnetic neural network to recognise patterns from human voice converted into spikes.
notes:
SEEDS/GROUNDING: from corpus-profile candidate vector-60 (spiking hardware). Candidate evidence SQL re-executed this pass: SELECT p.id,p.acronym FROM project p WHERE p.objective ILIKE '%spiking neural%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%spiking neuron%' OR p.title ILIKE '%spiking%' -> 17 rows, identical id list to the candidate (no drift). Objectives read in full for 687299, 705957, 707373, 715872, 724295, 732642, 747848, 753470, 780848, 794425, 824162, 826655, 828841, 871371, 871501, 876925, 658479, 705100, 773228, 788793, 694829, 695459, 713736, 785911, 871330, 888129, 956601, 101016734.
GOLD CRITERION (positive, applied evenly): the project's own work delivers physical computing hardware - a chip, integrated circuit, photonic or other fabricated device - in which the computation itself is carried by spikes/pulses fired between artificial (silicon, photonic, magnetic) neurons. Three consequences, applied to every project alike: (a) projects that model or simulate spiking neurons in software, or study spiking in biological tissue, are OUT; (b) neuromorphic/analog/in-memory hardware whose computation is not carried by neuron pulses (memristive or ferroelectric synapse materials on their own, oscillatory or reservoir computing, in-memory matrix multiplication) is OUT; (c) a project is OUT when the spiking computation it reports was run on neuromorphic hardware it did not itself deliver - whether the vehicle is a named external platform (ROLLS, Dynap-se, SCAMP, SpiNNaker) or an unnamed 'programmable neuromorphic substrate' - because in every such case the project's own deliverable is an algorithm, model, architecture or readout circuit rather than the spiking device. 707373 ECogNeT, 794425 STRoNA and 747848 ProbSenS are all excluded on this single ground.
POOLED ADJUDICATION (k=20, all four conditions, 40 distinct projects surfaced; index be84cbad9182). IN: 824162 SYNCH (silicon neural network of spiking neurons on a chip); 828841 ChipAI (nanophotonic neuron-like light-spiking sources/detectors); 724295 NeuroAgents (report: fabricated DYNAP-SE2, a mixed-signal Spiking Neuronal Network processor); 826655 TEMPO (hardware for SNN, dot-product/integrate-and-fire engines); 871371 MeM-Scales (analog spiking microprocessors); 963928 SOFT (designed, fabricated and tested a magnetic spiking neuron; magnetic neural network run on voice converted into spikes); 687299 NeuRAM3 (fabricate a chip with spike-based learning); 780848 Fun-COMP (hardware implementing spiking neural networks). OUT: 724822 CODE4Vision, 964877 NEU-ChiP, 701983 Neuroheart, 864243 ANewSpike, 665683 NeuroNanoChip, 897420 LAMININ, 896143 MOVIS, 797205 iNtoPoreAge, 714291 CONNEXIO, 852086 AGEMEC, 813851 ASCTN-Training, 865617 CELPRED, 658850 Als-on-a-chip, 755383 MwHresEP, 747598 3DMUCHO, 752819 ATiNaRI (all biological/neuroscience or neural-recording work, no artificial spiking hardware); 840903 FREEMIND, 892669 FAST, 861153 MANIC, 640003 NEURAMORPH, 802615 BIOMORPHIC, 820048 MY-CUBE, 818399 SPINAPSE, 899646 k-NET, 682955 bioSPINspired, 899559 SpinAge (spin/ferroelectric/organic neuromorphic devices, in-memory or oscillator computing; a regexp for spike/integrate-and-fire context over their full stored text returns nothing for SpinAge, whose only 'pulse' is laser irradiation for weight setting); 871501 NeurONN (oscillatory neural networks, phase-encoded, its own objective states the ONN gain is 'vs state of the art spiking neural network (SNN) architecture' - i.e. an explicit alternative to spikes); 788793 BACKUP (photonic reservoir computing interfaced to biological neurons; no spike or integrate-and-fire passage anywhere in its stored text); 101016734 MISEL (event-based neuromorphic vision circuits; text never states neuron pulses as the computation); 713736 NeuroPsense (builds a demonstrator around neuromorphic processors developed in another project; stored text contains no spike/firing/pulse language at all); 824164 HERMES (designed and fabricated a CMOS-neuron chip for a regenerative-medicine system; stored text contains no spike/firing/pulse language); 707373 ECogNeT and 794425 STRoNA (criterion (c): the spiking computation runs on ROLLS, Dynap-se, SCAMP and SpiNNaker, platforms built elsewhere, with the reported work largely in the Brian2 simulator).
NON-POOLED CANDIDATES ADJUDICATED FROM FULL TEXT (counted in pooled_candidate_count): IN - 715872 NANOINFER, 732642 ULPEC, 753470 NEPSpiNN, 876925 ANDANTE, 871737 BeFerroSynaptic; OUT - 747848 ProbSenS. pooled_candidate_count = 40 pooled projects + these 6 = 46; accepted 13 + rejected_count 33 = 46.
747848 ProbSenS, OUT under criterion (c): its own deliverable is a low-power event-driven probabilistic VLSI architecture for multisensor readout, and its objective never mentions spikes; the only spiking evidence is in the report - 'determined conversion and learning rules to run the algorithms in the spiking domain on a programmable neuromorphic substrate' and a ReLU-trained CNN 'converted to the spiking domain by using the open source snn toolbox'. The substrate it ran on is nowhere stated to be its own fabrication, which places it exactly where ECogNeT and STRoNA sit.
871737 BeFerroSynaptic, IN: report summary - 'Unlike the conventional vonNeumann architecture, that uses digital numbers for calculation, in our spiking neural networks the information is represented by event driven and correlated voltage spikes'; workPerformed - 'The 2BeFerro chip implements a Calcium-based learning rule by utilizing 64 Exp-I&F neurons with one learning synapse each' and 'our high-complexity demonstrator TEXEL is a 9mm x 9mm neuromorphic chip that was designed using the xfab 180nm xp018 technology. The chip features 180 adaptive-exponential integrate and fire (AdExp-I&F) neurons, each receiving input from 58 synapses... TEXEL chips have been packaged and functionality was verified.' A fabricated, packaged integrate-and-fire chip - the positive criterion met. (This entry corrects an earlier draft note that rejected 871737 as a ferroelectric device project with no spike-based computation; that reason was false against its stored text.)
899598 PHEMTRONICS, OUT: its report summary names an 'all-optical spiking neuron circuit, with integrated all-optical synapses' among the device classes the project is developing, but workPerformed and finalResults deliver phase-change plasmonic switches, modulators, photodetectors and materials work - the spiking neuron circuit is named in the aims and not reported as delivered. Same shape as the 785911 SHADOKS exclusion.
CLASS-B RE-READ (all eight projects whose only spike-family term sits in the report were re-checked against their own text this pass): 871737 BeFerroSynaptic -> moved to gold (above); 747848 ProbSenS -> OUT under (c) (above); 899598 PHEMTRONICS -> OUT, aims-not-delivered (above); 841995 RESWITCH -> OUT, its spike mentions are plasticity rules in resistive-switching materials ('emulating the time-dependent dynamics of biological synapses such as spike-rate and spike timing dependent plasticity (SRDP and STDP)'), a synapse-material project with no spiking computation; 773228 IONOS -> OUT, no spike or integrate-and-fire passage anywhere in its stored text, deliverable is iono-electronic devices for interfacing with living cells; 788793 BACKUP -> OUT, no spike or integrate-and-fire passage, photonic reservoir computing; 899559 SpinAge -> OUT, no spike or integrate-and-fire passage, spin-oscillator neuromorphic system; 707373 ECogNeT -> OUT under (c).
COMPLETENESS SWEEP (regexp_matches, not LIKE; over lower(title||objective||report_text.teaser||summary||workPerformed||finalResults), hyphenated/spaced/closed variants covered). Patterns swept, with corpus-wide counts: 'spiking neural|spiking-neural|spikingneural' 28; 'spiking neuron|spiking-neuron' 14; 'spike-based|spike based|spike-driven|spike driven|spike coding|spike-coding' 3; 'neuromorphic' 135; 'memristive synap|memristor synap|artificial synap|synaptic device' 16; 'silicon neuron|artificial neuron|neuron circuit' 18; 'brain-inspired|brain inspired|brain-like|neuro-inspired|neuro inspired' 50; SNN as a token 14; 'event-driven|event driven|event-based|event based' 81; 'spiking' anywhere 95; 'integrate-and-fire|integrate and fire|leaky integrate' also swept. The spike-family + neuromorphic union is 205 projects (106 with the term in title/objective, 99 in report text only). Partition, every member adjudicated: (A) 42 with a spike-family term in title/objective - individually triaged, gold drawn from here plus SOFT; the rest are neuroscience/biology (e.g. 633428 EngineeringPercepts, 679253 HIRESMEMMANIP, 101030918 AutoMIND, 101032806 NeuralFieldTheoriES, 658479 SpikeControl, 705100 BIOMODULAR - spiking-network models, simulations and theory, no hardware built) or non-spiking devices (705957 SelectX - memristor/MEMS crossbar; its only 'spiking' is a biological analogy). (B) 8 with 'neuromorphic' in title/objective and a spike term only in the report - all re-read this pass, dispositions listed under CLASS-B RE-READ above. (C) 49 with a spike term in report text only and no 'neuromorphic' anywhere in title/objective - all listed and reviewed with their spike context; every one is biological/neuroscience or unrelated (e.g. 785911 SHADOKS - nanofluidic device showing autonomous spiking, computation named only as an ultimate goal; 956601 TEVI - time-encoded circuits explicitly 'mimicking the performance of spiking neural networks' without spikes; 695459 Milli-Tech - 'terahertz spiking detectors', a switch-physics detector; 813713 NeuTouch - an SNN used as an algorithm) except 963928 SOFT, which is IN. (D) 106 projects carrying 'neuromorphic' (or the wider brain-inspired/event-driven families) with no spike-family term anywhere in their stored text - rejected as a class, mechanically: a project whose ~8k characters of stored text never mention spikes, spiking, SNN or spike-based operation does not state that its hardware computes with spikes; these are materials, memristive/ferroelectric/spintronic device, photonic and in-memory-computing projects. The class was re-probed for spike-free pulse language ('(neuron|neural) within 200 chars of firing|fires|fire|pulses'): 3 hits, all checked - 818179 EngineeringBAP (ultrasound pulses in brain therapy), 101007926 neuronsXnets (firing probability of cortical neurons), 101032701 MIETMAN (fabricated memristors used to realise a leak-integrate-and-fire model; a single device-level neuron emulation inside a 2D-materials transport-modelling project, no spiking computation carried out - deliberate near-miss).
DELIBERATE NEAR-MISSES (the discrimination boundary): 871501 NeurONN, 705957 SelectX, 101032701 MIETMAN, 785911 SHADOKS, 899598 PHEMTRONICS, 713736 NeuroPsense, 824164 HERMES, 707373 ECogNeT, 794425 STRoNA, 747848 ProbSenS, 658479 SpikeControl, 679253 HIRESMEMMANIP, 101030918 AutoMIND, 101032806 NeuralFieldTheoriES.
TERM_STYLE: paraphrase. The question uses none of the gold texts' key vocabulary - no 'spiking', 'spike', 'neuromorphic', 'SNN', 'event-based', 'memristive' - and describes the mechanism instead ('artificial neurons compute by firing brief pulses at each other, the way nerve cells do'). The rank matrix supports this: lexical's top-ranked projects are biological (724822 CODE4Vision rank 1, 788793 BACKUP rank 2) and 5 of the 13 gold projects (NANOINFER, ULPEC, NEPSpiNN, ANDANTE, BeFerroSynaptic) are outside every condition's top-20, while the gold projects that do surface come mostly through dense/hybrid (826655 TEMPO dense-only, 687299 NeuRAM3 dense 9, 724295 NeuroAgents dense 3).
TEXT-NOT-SQL: no stored column encodes 'computes with spikes'; the euroSciVoc tag for these projects is generic electrical/electronic engineering, which also carries the Human Brain Project and unrelated device physics.

text: Which projects have the development or production of bacteriophages as an antibacterial product or treatment among their stated objectives, where the phages are applied to kill bacteria in human patients, livestock, crops or food rather than in environmental settings such as wastewater, and where the phage work is not merely an investigative strand under some other objective?
reference_answer: Eight projects set out to make bacteriophages themselves into an antibacterial product. For patients: PhagoPROD scales up the GMP manufacturing and GLP diagnostics behind Pherecydes Pharma's personalised phage therapy against antibiotic-resistant infections; PHARMS screens phages of resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, Helicobacter pylori and Haemophilus influenzae and engineers phage vectors into a battery of phage-based therapies; and CURE builds phage preparations as candidates for clinical testing in asthma, using phages to rebalance a dysbiotic airway microbiome. For animals and food: AVANT tests veterinary medicinal products containing bacteriophages and polymers against enterotoxigenic E. coli diarrhoea in weaning pigs, PHAGOVET develops a biocide plus two food-additive products based on selected bacteriophages to control Salmonella and E. coli in poultry production, and AntiCamp develops a spray of phage-based particles that inject antibacterial genes into Campylobacter jejuni for food decontamination. For crops: PhageFire develops a phage-cocktail biopesticide against fire blight (Erwinia amylovora) in pome fruit, and VIROPLANT reports accomplishing initial steps to bring to the European market the first phage cocktail for a crop disease. What unites them is that producing the phage is the objective and the phage is the product; they are a small applied minority among the corpus's many phage projects, most of which instead study phage biology, phage-host coevolution or bacterial anti-phage defence systems.
notes: SEEDS (from cp6 candidate vector-52, sample ids re-read this pass): 811749 PhagoPROD, 958645 PhageFire, 773567 VIROPLANT kept as gold; 817842 CoPathoPhage, 896441 ERA, 656647 MicroEcoEvol read and rejected. Candidate drift check re-executed: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM project p WHERE p.objective ILIKE '%phage therapy%' OR p.title ILIKE '%phage therapy%' -> 11, matching the recorded evidence. ADJUDICATION RULE (now carried on the face of the question): IN iff (a) developing or producing bacteriophages as an antibacterial agent is among the project's own stated objectives, (b) the phages are applied against bacteria in human patients, livestock, crops or food - not in environmental settings such as wastewater, and (c) the phage work is not merely an investigative strand under some other objective. OUT: studying phage biology, phage-host coevolution or bacterial anti-phage defence; phage display as a discovery tool; phage-DERIVED molecules (endolysins, pyocins, autolysin motifs) rather than phages; phages as surrogates or indicators; phages taken off the shelf as an unmodified payload with no development or production of the phage; phages screened only in report text as one interchangeable antimicrobial among several. COMPLETENESS SWEEP (regexp_matches, not LIKE, over lower(title||objective||report_text.teaser||summary||workPerformed||finalResults)): universe = word-bounded phage|bacteriophage|phagotherap|endolysin|lysin -> 129 projects (word boundary keeps macrophage/autophagy out); per-project flags also computed for phage[ -]?therap, phagotherap, bacteriophage, phage cocktail|cocktail of phage, lytic phage|virulent phage, phage[ -]based|phage[ -]derived|phage[ -]encoded, endolysin|lysin|phage lysin. Applied-context co-occurrence sweep narrowed 129 -> 49 for full reading; the 12 residual projects whose phage mention sat outside that window (833594 PHAS, 955664 STIMULUS, 811249 ProtectedDairy, 817526 PRE-HLB, 658701 ImmunoFarm, 745791 REFUCOAT, 813439 BREAK BIOFILMS, 670216 MYCOCHASSIS, 101016174 CleanAir among them) were checked by extracting a 270-char context window around every phage mention. ADJUDICATED UNIVERSE = 129 swept + 5 pooled candidates outside the sweep (772853 ENTRAPMENT from the first pooled run; 655398 ARBUATEM, 714224 MIX-Effectors, 818431 SIMBA, 774078 Pharma-Factory from the second) = 134; accepted 8, rejected 126. Those 5 contain no phage/bacteriophage/endolysin/lysin token anywhere in title, objective or report text - the sweep's own result rules them out of a phage-product question - and their titles show why they surfaced (antibiotic-resistant bacteria in urban agriculture; T6SS effectors as antibacterial treatment; microbiome applications in food; plant molecular factories). POOLED RUN (final wording, all four conditions at k=20, union 30 projects, index be84cbad9182): 6 of the 8 gold appear - PhagoPROD lex 5 / dense 8 / hyb 3 / rerank 4; PHARMS 6/7/8/16; AntiCamp 11/4/4/17; PHAGOVET 15/3/5/7; PhageFire 12/12/15/6; VIROPLANT -/14/-/-. CURE (767015) and AVANT (862829) appear in NO condition's top-20 and are gold from the completeness sweep plus a full read of their text. DELIBERATE NEAR-MISSES: 101029908 GELNANODEP (gel depot loaded natural bacteriophages as an off-the-shelf second payload under a melanoma-treatment objective; no development, selection or production of phages anywhere in its record - fails criteria (a) and (c), and contrasts with PHAGOVET's 'based on selected bacteriophages' and PhageFire's cocktail development); 873591 StaphIMPACT (Micreos SA.100 is an endolysin product - phage-derived enzyme, no phage administered); 705817 PYANO (retargeted pyocins carrying phage receptor-binding proteins, phage-derived protein not phages); 101025065 NanoBioRS (implant coatings; report work on delivery of chimeric phage endolysins); 850936 PANDORA (mycobacteriophage autolysin binding sequence grafted into fusion antibodies); 836754 SaPhaDe (characterises Salmonella anti-phage defences to inform phage-therapeutic design, develops no phage product); 817842 CoPathoPhage (prophage-pathogen cooperation in mammalian infection; therapy named only as a downstream hope); 101026675 Phage POWER and 792686 ENVIROSTOME (phages against bacteria in wastewater and aquatic environments - excluded by criterion (b)); 799417 NoPHAME (phages as surrogates for mammalian viruses in wastewater inactivation assays); 765147 CARTNET (AMR training network whose phage strand is an investigative element under a non-phage objective - excluded by criterion (c); it is the hardest distractor, ranking 10th on rerank and 16th on lexical); 833594 PHAS, 955664 STIMULUS, 745791 REFUCOAT, 813439 BREAK BIOFILMS (bandage, stimuli-responsive material, food packaging, antifouling interface: bacteriophages or phage-derived products appear in report text as one of several antimicrobial candidates screened for a platform whose aim is the material); 811249 ProtectedDairy (protects starter cultures FROM phages - opposite direction); 884988 DYNAMIC and 656647 MicroEcoEvol (phage ecology that names future phage therapy in aquaculture / bloom control as an implication). POOLED REJECTS across both runs (best chunk or full text shows study-not-product, or no phage at all): 836754, 101003229 DEFEND, 747527 EvoMachine-Phage, 705817, 845658 CO-DEfENDENCE, 681203 PhageResist, 884988, 659314 ROPHARE, 714478 EVOIMMECH, 865694 DiversiPHI, 819800 BIONICbacteria, 101026675, 817842, 660039 PHAGECOM, 834052 anti-CRISPR, 716734 BIOFAGE, 765147, 772853 ENTRAPMENT, 865849 CAPSID, 757563 PRO_PHAGE, 101018520 DefenseAgainstPhage, 842656 PredProkDef, 833594, 792686, 799417, 655398, 714224, 818431, 774078, 101002643 ECOSTRAT, 794447 ProphARG, 101001684 PHAGENET. The remaining swept projects are rejected as phage display / phage-derived antibody or peptide libraries (e.g. 779802 ITHACA, 840232 microPhage, 764434 PRe-ART, 886470 CAESAR, 101020521 TARGET, 658701 ImmunoFarm), CRISPR and prokaryotic-defence mechanism work (639707 REMEMBER, 753528 Anti-CRISPR, 844093 GenDels, 818878 CRISPRsition, 788405 EPICut, 845268 MSOPGDM, 101018608 CBASS), phage or virome ecology and horizontal-gene-transfer studies (646868 PhageDiff, 715772 BabyVir, 750779 COEXIST, 101032316 CessOmics, 895167 MiMoZa, 101025891 REDTEAR), or a single incidental phage mention in an unrelated project (e.g. 649021 BIOMENDELIAN, 657076 HJMIGRA, 731868 VIRUSCAN, 771567 CABUM, 773649 Circular Agronomics). TERM_STYLE exact-term: the question reuses the gold texts' own vocabulary - 'phage therapy' (PhagoPROD title), 'bacteriophages' (PHAGOVET, AVANT), 'phage-based' (AntiCamp title, PHARMS), 'phage cocktail' (PhageFire, VIROPLANT) - and lexical BM25 ranks five gold projects inside its top-20 (PhagoPROD 5, PHARMS 6, AntiCamp 11, PhageFire 12, PHAGOVET 15), which the heuristic reads as real term overlap.
